summary: Lucien Lévy-Bruhl was a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. He studied at the École Normale Supérieure (~1876-1879) and the Sorbonne (~1879-1884). He founded and held a post at the University of Paris (~1899-1927) and taught Paul Mus.

Lucien Tesniere was a linguist who studied at the University of Paris, University of Leipzig, École des Langues Orientales, and under Antoine Meillet (~1913-1920). He held posts at the University of Ljubljana (~1921-1924), University of Strasbourg (1924-1937), and University of Montpellier (1937).

Lucy Annette Jones is a scholar in tibetology and religious studies. She earned her PhD at Rice University under doctoral supervisors Anne Carolyn Klein and Edith Wyschogrod, and studied under Tenzin Wangyal Rinpoche from 1996 to 1997.

Ludo Rocher was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Ghent University, SOAS, and under scholars including Adriaan Scharpé and Jan Gonda. He served at the Free University of Brussels (1959-1966) and as Chair at the University of Pennsylvania (1966-2002).

Ludwig Alsdorf was an indologist and scholar of Buddhist studies. He studied at Heidelberg, Hamburg (PhD under Walther Schubring), and Berlin (habilitation under Heinrich Lüders). His career included posts at Allahabad, Berlin, Münster, and a professorship at the University of Hamburg (1950-1972).

Ludwig Diestel was a scholar of religious studies and linguistics who studied under Heinrich Ewald (~1845-1847). He held posts at the universities of Bonn (~1858-1862), Greifswald (~1862-1867), Jena (~1867-1872), and Tübingen (~1872-1879).

Ludwig Heller was an indologist and linguist who earned his Dr. phil. under Franz Kielhorn at Göttingen (1887-1893) and habilitated at Greifswald (~1895-1897). He held posts at the Prussian State Library (1893), Greifswald (1904), and Tartu (1918).

Ludwig Lange was a scholar in philosophy and other fields who studied at Göttingen under Theodor Benfey (~1843-1847) and at Leipzig. He held posts at Göttingen (~1850-1855), Prague (~1855-1859), Giessen (~1859-1871), and Leipzig (~1871-1885).

Ludwig Wittgenstein was a philosopher who studied at TH Berlin, Manchester, and Cambridge (PhD ~1929). He taught K. N. Jayatilleke and held posts at Cambridge as a lecturer and fellow at Trinity College (1929-1947) and Professor of Philosophy (1930-1947).
Ludwik Skurzak was an indologist who studied under Stanisław Schayer and worked as a lecturer at the University of Breslau.

Luigi Suali was a scholar in Indology and philosophy who studied at the University of Bologna (~1899-1903) and under Hermann Jacobi (~1904-1906). He held a post at the University of Pavia from circa 1907 to 1951.

Luis Oscar Gómez was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at the University of Puerto Rico, Yale (under Stanley Insler), and Michigan. He chaired Asian languages at Michigan (attested 1977-2012) and was Academic Director at Mangalam Research Center.

Luise Hercus was an Indologist and linguist who studied at St Anne's College and Australian National University. She held posts as tutor and lecturer at St Anne's College (1948-1954), researcher at Adelaide (1965-1969), and academic positions at ANU (1969, 1991).
Lungten Dubgyur is a scholar of Tibetology and law. He completed his studies at Sherubtse College, Government Law College in Mumbai (LL.B), and the University of Edinburgh (LL.M).

Lungtok Tenpai Nyima was a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who earned a Geshe degree at Kyangtsang Monastery under Tendzin Lodro Gyatso. He lectured at the University of Oslo (1967) and founded Menri Monastery, serving as abbot from 1969.
Lungtok Tenpé Nyima was a scholar who studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.

Lutz Bieg is a sinologist who earned his Dr. phil. at the University of Heidelberg (~1966-1971) and habilitated at the Free University of Berlin (1986). He served as a professor of Chinese studies at the University of Cologne (1989-2008).

Lynn Struve is a scholar in sinology and history/archaeology. She studied at the University of Washington (~1963-1967) and the University of Michigan (~1967-1974), and held a post at Indiana University from circa 1977 to 2010.

Lynn Thomas is an indologist and religious studies scholar. She completed a BA and MA at Lancaster University and earned a D. Phil at the University of Oxford in 1987, later serving as lecturer in Hinduism at the University of Roehampton (attested 1997).

Léon Feer was a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies who studied under Philippe Édouard Foucaux and Etienne Marc Quatremère. He held posts at INALCO (1865), Collège de France (1869-1872), and the Bibliothèque nationale de France (1872, 1900).
